text: What is the main purpose of the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account?
options: To determine the profit or loss of the firm
To distribute the profits among the partners
To show the financial position of the firm
To calculate the capital of the partners
correctAnswer: To distribute the profits among the partners
explanation: The Profit and Loss Appropriation Account is prepared to distribute the profits among the partners in their profit-sharing ratio. It is a necessary step in the process of accounting for partnership.

text: Which of the following is not a method of charging interest on partners' capital?
options: Interest on capital out of profits
Interest on drawings out of profits
Interest on capital out of capital
Interest on capital out of reserve
correctAnswer: Interest on capital out of capital
explanation: Interest on capital out of capital is not a method of charging interest on partners' capital. Interest on capital out of profits is a method where interest is charged on the capital of the partners out of the profits of the firm.

text: What is the formula for calculating interest on drawings?
options: $\frac{D \times R \times T}{100}$
$\frac{D \times R \times T}{365}$
$\frac{D \times R \times T}{360}$
$\frac{D \times R \times T}{12}$
explanation: The formula for calculating interest on drawings is $\frac{D \times R \times T}{365}$, where D is the amount of drawings, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.
